## Appearance

Gilbert Blythe is a tall, broad-shouldered young man with a frank face and curly brown hair. He has hazel, clear, and straightforward eyes that carry a roguish, half-shy, and half-eager expression. His mouth is often twisted into a teasing smile, giving him a manly appearance.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever, good-natured, and thoughtful young man with his own distinct thoughts and a strong drive to get the best out of life while contributing his best in return. He aims to do honest, real work in the world by becoming a doctor to fight disease, pain, and ignorance, though he sometimes finds himself torn between his genuine convictions and his desire to meet Anne's ideal.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. ## History

Gilbert Blythe returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) after spending time with his cousins in [New Brunswick](../codex/places.md#new-brunswick) and three years in Alberta with his sick father. Upon his return to school, he inadvertently sparked a long-standing feud with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) after pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots," prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his attempts to apologize. Over the next few years, Gilbert engaged in an intense academic rivalry with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) through their common school term and their time in Miss Stacy's Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) preparation class. After sparking Anne's determination at a benefit concert performance, he pursued the First Class course alongside her at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), where he ultimately won the class medal. Following [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) Cuthbert's death, Gilbert generously gave up his teaching post at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school so [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) could take the position and remain at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). This selflessness led [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to forgive him, and the two reconciled into close friends. Together, they established and led the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society), navigating various community setbacks, such as a severe hail storm that destroyed their planted trees. Gilbert later rejoiced when Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) moved into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), as it freed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to leave her teaching role and attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) with him. After walking [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) home from Miss Lavendar's garden wedding, Gilbert shared a quiet moment with her, signaling a subtle romantic shift in their evolving relationship.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> “All right!” Gilbert sprang into his skiff with an angry color in his cheeks. “I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley. And I don’t care either!”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P34](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0034)

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

> "but wouldn’t it have been more beautiful still, Anne, if there had been NO separation or misunderstanding . . . if they had come hand in hand all the way through life, with no memories behind them but those which belonged to each other?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 XXX A Wedding at the Stone House P39](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0039)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert's relationship with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) began in childhood when he tried to get her attention by calling her 'Carrots,' leading [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to smash a slate over his head and hold a long grudge. Despite Gilbert saving her from a leaking boat on the pond and offering an apology, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) initially cold-shouldered his attempts to end their feud. Over time, their dynamic evolved from sharp academic rivalry into mutual reconciliation, as the two became fellow teachers and close friends who candidly share their ambitions.

- Friend of — reconciled childhood friends and study partners  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. - Saved — rescued her from bridge pile using dory  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P26](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0026), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P38](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0038)</sub>

### [Shirley](../character/shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/gilbert-blythe--shirley.md)

Gilbert initially shared an intense academic rivalry with [Shirley](../character/shirley.md), competing closely for top marks throughout their school years at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). This academic competition eventually transitioned into a warm friendship as they grew older. By the time they finished their teaching terms, Gilbert was delighted by the news of Shirley's plans, and their bond deepened into a close companionship marked by shared walks and subtle romantic feelings.

- Rival of — intense academic rivalry for top marks in school  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036)</sub>
- Friend of — friendship (since v2)  <sub>[v2 XXVI Around the Bend P46](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0046), [v2 XXX A Wedding at the Stone House P40](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0040)</sub>

### [Charlie Sloane](../character/charlie-sloane.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/charlie-sloane--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert and Charlie are schoolmates who belong to the same peer group in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea). The two are presumed to be rivals competing for the good graces and attention of [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md). Beyond their shared classroom history and mutual acquaintance with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), their interactions are defined by this unspoken competition.

- presumed Rival of — rivals for the good graces of Anne Shirley (since v2)  <sub>[v2 XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country P0](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0000)</sub>

### [Fred Wright](../character/fred-wright.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/fred-wright--gilbert-blythe.md)
